column1: # Runtime voice: lines that only exist in game, because they hold real values. Piper speaks them, no audio is built.
# UTF-8, tab separated, # starts a comment line. Add a row and restart KSP, that is all.
# id       a-z 0-9 _, starts with rt_, unique
# kind     report (now and then), dock (after a docking approach call), land (once per descent, low and falling),
#          science, science_pts (after a science reaction), contract_funds, contract_done, contract_failed
#          chat: an intercom chat between two kerbals. Id rt_chat_<name>_<seq>, one row per line, seq 1, 2, 3.
#          Kerbal A speaks the odd lines, kerbal B the even ones. Only line 1 has a when.
# when     empty or any: always. A situation (orbit flight suborbital landed escape) and/or checks like fuel<25
#          or node_min>=2. Several situations: one must match. Every check must hold.
#          In a chat also the job of a kerbal: a=pilot (kerbal A, who starts) and/or b=scientist (kerbal B).
#          Jobs: pilot engineer scientist tourist. The chat only plays when the two kerbals have those jobs, in
#          either order: if only B has the job of a, B starts. A kerbal with a job from a mod fits no job check.
# spanish  normal Spanish. A number slot becomes Spanish words, reversed like every other word (loñapsE).
#          A name slot is spoken as the name. Write the number before a masculine noun: "un" for 1 is made.
# english  the subtitle. A number slot shows digits, a name slot the name.
# Number slots: alt_km pe_km ap_km speed fuel day sci funds inc_deg period_min t_ap_min t_pe_min ec mono parts
#   crew node_dv node_min funds_total sci_total rep contracts dist_m close_ms height_m vspeed_ms
#   at_home flight_no missions stars visits landings (crew history, see below)
#   (km, min, deg, ms and sci get one decimal below 10, the rest whole numbers)
# Name slots: vessel body exp target, and in a chat self (the speaker) and other (the one spoken to)
# Crew history: in a report {kerbal} is the kerbal Mission Control talks to, and these numbers are that kerbal's.
#   In a chat they are the numbers of kerbal A (who starts). flight_no (this flight, 1 is the first), missions
#   (flights that ended with a recovery), visits and landings (earlier flights that reached or landed on this body),
#   stars (experience level). at_home is 1 at Kerbin, else 0. A template that uses them only plays with crew aboard.
# Avoid a plural noun after a value that can be 1: use a check like node_min>=2.
